clue.text: Military supporter affected to flourish, circling round line

parts.note: camp means theatrically affected or mannered

indicators.note: the flourish word goes around the next two pieces, so it surrounds them

parts.note: to flower is to flourish or bloom
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A soldier's backer puts on airs and prospers while going round a line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circling' puts O and L inside FLOWER, after its F, to give FOLLOWER.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically, civilians who trailed an army to sell goods or services were known as camp followers, and the phrase now means any hanger-on.

clue.text: Church took in gold from castle

parts.note: took in as in consumed food means ate
AU is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A church absorbed gold from a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: A chateau is a French castle or grand country house.

clue.text: End of game fellow?

explanation.definitionFit: Checkmate ends a chess game, often shortened, and a fellow or pal is a British and Australian mate.

clue.text: Male often in hot spot shows anger over male in cool

indicators.note: in means these pieces go inside the cooling word

parts.note: a fan cools you

indicators.note: over in a down clue puts the first piece above the next

parts.note: ire means anger

explanation.surface: A man in a hot place loses his temper over another man trying to keep cool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' places IRE above M in this down clue, and 'in' puts IREM inside FAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A firefighter regularly works close to flames, and fireman is the traditional term.

clue.text: Inclination not to start the dusting?

indicators.note: not to start means drop the first letter

parts.note: dusting is part of the cleaning

explanation.surface: A reluctance to begin the housework.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaning is a tendency or preference.

clue.text: Farm produce from layers? Not chickens, principally

indicators.note: not tells you to remove a letter

parts.note: coats are layers, as of paint

indicators.note: principally means take the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Eggs from hens? Not mostly from chickens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'layers' looks like egg-laying hens but means coats; 'Not' removes the first letter of chickens.
explanation.definitionFit: Oats are a cereal crop grown on farms.

clue.text: Working legs in hard race

indicators.note: working means the letters are worked over into a new order

parts.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Legs pumping hard during a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working' rearranges LEGS and IN into ENGLIS.
explanation.definitionFit: The English are a people or nation, an old sense of race.

clue.text: Initially how one plays Monopoly…

parts.note: in the board game every player starts on the square marked GO

explanation.surface: A clue about how a board game begins.
explanation.walkthrough: Monopoly is a property-trading board game whose starting square is GO.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means right from the very beginning.

clue.text: … while at Greenwich?

parts.note: Greenwich in London gives its name to Greenwich Mean Time

explanation.surface: Something happening at the London observatory.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to 7-down. Greenwich sets GMT, so to be at Greenwich is to be in the mean time.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean during the period in between.

clue.text: Source of energy that's about thespian

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a thespian is an actor

explanation.surface: A power source said to concern a stage performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear reactor is a plant that generates power.

clue.text: Eating disorders, produced by new body chemical

indicators.note: disorders as a verb says the letters of the preceding word are jumbled

explanation.surface: Eating disorders seem to be triggered by some new chemical in the body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eating disorders' reads as a medical phrase, but 'disorders' is a verb telling you to scramble EATING into ANTIGE.
explanation.definitionFit: An antigen is a substance that provokes an immune response in the body.

clue.text: Suitable encounter

explanation.definitionFit: Meet is an old word for proper or fitting, and as a verb it means come across someone.

clue.text: Opening moves exhibiting no good range

indicators.note: no tells you to leave out the letter for good

parts.note: a gambit is an opening sequence of moves in chess

explanation.surface: Chess openings with no merit cover a certain range.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambit means the scope or extent of something.

clue.text: Not entirely attractive meal

indicators.note: not entirely means the word is cut short, dropping its final letter

parts.note: dishy is informal British for good-looking

explanation.surface: A meal that isn't wholly appealing.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish is a prepared serving of food.

clue.text: Boards the coach

explanation.definitionFit: The theatre is called the boards, and a stagecoach is a horse-drawn coach.

clue.text: Name dropping in affectation, displaying offensive attitude

indicators.note: dropping in means the letter falls inside the other word

parts.note: side is British slang for pretension, putting on airs

explanation.surface: Name-dropping by a pretentious person shows a nasty attitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Name dropping' reads as the social habit, but N for Name drops into SIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Snide means sneering and mean-spirited.

clue.text: Excited about involving American city

indicators.note: involving means the first pieces wrap around the next one

parts.note: hot means excited or eager
on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled about an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' puts US inside HOTON, after HO.
explanation.definitionFit: Houston is a large city in Texas.

clue.text: Stuff that's found in bulging hamburgers

indicators.note: found in says the letters sit inside the following words

explanation.surface: Something discovered inside overstuffed burgers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuff' is the definition in its sense of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Gingham is a checked cotton fabric, and stuff is an old word for cloth.

clue.text: Mistakenly showing mocking humour about long upset

indicators.note: about means the humour word goes around the next piece

parts.note: wry describes dry, mocking humour

indicators.note: upset means the letters of long are knocked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wrongly shows sarcasm about a prolonged upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns LONG into RONGL, and 'about' puts that inside WRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrongly means in error, which is what mistakenly says.

clue.text: Go on for longer than a route snaking around West

indicators.note: around means the scrambled letters go round the next piece
snaking means twisting about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A road winds westwards for a long way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snaking' turns A ROUTE into OUTEAR, and 'around' wraps it round W.
explanation.definitionFit: To outwear something is to last longer than it.

clue.text: One guy upset Right, being less experienced

indicators.note: upset means the letters are tipped over into a new order

explanation.surface: A man gets upset by the Right, being greener.
explanation.definitionFit: Younger people have usually had fewer years to gain experience.

clue.text: Island that is seen from behind in most of Indian city

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other
most of means drop the last letter

parts.note: Madras is the former name of Chennai in India

indicators.note: seen from behind means the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: ie abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: An island viewed from the rear inside most of a city in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen from behind' turns IE into EI, which goes 'in' MADRA ('most of' MADRAS).
explanation.definitionFit: Madeira is an Atlantic island belonging to Portugal.

clue.text: What's the point of a story about a yard belonging to the council leader?

indicators.note: about means the lesson word goes round the next pieces

parts.words: What's the point of a story
parts.note: the moral is the lesson a story teaches

explanation.surface: A fable's lesson about a yard owned by the town's leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A and Y inside MORAL, after its M.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayoral describes things of or relating to a mayor, who leads a council.

clue.text: Some swimmers evidently do so

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Swimmers clearly plunge in.
explanation.definitionFit: To immerse oneself is to go under water, which swimmers do.

clue.text: Biblical heroine in reality decapitated

indicators.note: decapitated means the head, the first letter, is cut off

parts.note: truth means reality or fact

explanation.surface: An Old Testament heroine beheaded in real life.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruth is the loyal Moabite woman whose story has its own book in the Bible.

clue.text: Hydrocarbon? Best use this yellow liquid for starters

indicators.note: for starters means take the first letter of each of these words

explanation.surface: A chemistry tip: this yellow liquid is ideal.
explanation.definitionFit: Butyl is a four-carbon group derived from butane, a hydrocarbon; the question mark admits it is a group rather than a compound.

clue.text: Put out while withdrawing

indicators.note: withdrawing means drawing back, so the word is turned backwards

parts.note: a while is a period of time

explanation.surface: Extinguished while retreating.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit is to give off or send out.

clue.text: A stroke from the whip appears endless, unfortunately

indicators.note: endless means drop the last letter

parts.note: a lash is a blow from a whip

explanation.surface: A whiplash that seems unending, sadly.
explanation.definitionFit: Alas is an exclamation of regret.

clue.text: Continent has a former name of a local country curtailed

indicators.note: curtailed means cut short, losing the tail letter

parts.words: former name of a local country
parts.note: Siam was the old name of Thailand, in that continent

explanation.surface: A continent's old country name, shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia is the largest continent.

clue.text: Goose suitable for Birdman of Alcatraz in later life?

parts.words: suitable for Birdman of Alcatraz in later life
parts.note: the Birdman of Alcatraz was a long-term prisoner; in old age he would be a grey-haired convict, lag being slang for convict

explanation.surface: A goose that would suit an aged famous bird-keeping convict.
explanation.walkthrough: The Birdman of Alcatraz was Robert Stroud, a prisoner who kept birds; LAG is British slang for a convict, and an old one is GREY.
explanation.definitionFit: The greylag is a large grey wild goose, ancestor of most farmyard geese.

clue.text: Platform? Run out and play the guitar

parts.note: RO is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out
to strum is to play a guitar by brushing the strings

explanation.surface: A stage: run off and play some guitar.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batter dismissed 'run out' is scored as RO.
explanation.definitionFit: A rostrum is a raised stand for a speaker.

clue.text: Item for article in The Independent giving advice to parachutists?

definitions.text: Item for article in The Independent

parts.note: the phrase read as an instruction tells a skydiver to push the button that opens the chute

explanation.surface: A newspaper item that doubles as tips for skydivers.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words of instruction, a parachutist is told to press the release.
explanation.definitionFit: A statement issued to newspapers is often the basis of an article.
